messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At 10 kPa (≈0.1 atm) the freezing point of pure water drops below 0 °C.  
Using the water phase‑diagram (or the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the solid–liquid transition), the freezing point at 10 kPa is about **–2.2 °C** (≈ −2.2 °C ± 0.1 °C depending on the reference data set).  

So, under a pressure of 10 kPa, water will freeze at roughly –2.2 °C.
